name: Backtesting Engine
description: Build a backtesting engine that charges costs, refuses to peek, and reports honestly.

lessonNames.l14-too-good: A Sharpe above 2 is a bug
lessonNames.l15-how-many-settings: How many settings did you try?

lessonObjectives.l1-one-bar-at-a-time: Design an event loop that can only see past data.
lessonObjectives.l2-data-layer: Build a data layer that caches prices to disk.
lessonObjectives.l3-signal-to-position: Separate signals, target positions and orders.
lessonObjectives.l4-accounting: Track cash, holdings and equity correctly through every trade.
lessonObjectives.l5-next-open: Fill orders at a price the strategy could really have got.
lessonObjectives.l6-commissions-and-spread: Charge commissions and half the bid-ask spread on every trade.
lessonObjectives.l7-slippage: Add slippage that grows with order size.
lessonObjectives.l8-catching-look-ahead: Write a test that fails if the engine ever peeks at the future.
lessonObjectives.l9-sharpe: Compute an annualised Sharpe ratio correctly.
lessonObjectives.l10-drawdown-calmar: Compute maximum drawdown and the Calmar ratio.
lessonObjectives.l11-turnover: Measure turnover and estimate what it costs.
lessonObjectives.l12-benchmark: Compare a strategy with buy and hold on the same data.
lessonObjectives.l13-locked-away: Reserve an out-of-sample period and use it exactly once.
lessonObjectives.l14-too-good: Hunt for bugs in a backtest that looks too good.
lessonObjectives.l15-how-many-settings: Report how many parameter settings you tried and the spread of their results.
lessonObjectives.l16-results-note: Write a one-page results note, including what failed.
